problem: VLN research and LLM-based navigators like NavGPT are almost entirely English-only; Arabic (400M+ speakers) is absent from VLN benchmarks (R2R, RxR), and it is unknown how small or Arabic-centric LMs plan for navigation in Arabic.
motivation: Multilingual autonomous systems matter in the MENA region, but Arabic-trained models and datasets are scarce. SLMs are cheap and deployable on resource-limited robots, yet they are under-studied for navigation planning. The paper asks whether instruction language or model capability drives zero-shot VLN planning.
key_idea: Translate R2R instructions, observations and object lists into Arabic with an LLM, then run several small multilingual LMs and the Arabic-centric Jais 30B zero-shot inside the NavGPT framework to compare English and Arabic planning.
insight: Model capability and multilingual training matter more than input language: GPT-4o mini gets similar SR in English (21.0) and Arabic (20.0), while gaps between models are far larger. The Arabic-centric Jais gets 0 SR in both languages, so Arabic specialisation without instruction and navigation tuning does not help. Many failures are parsing and format errors and context-window overruns (Phi-3 completes only 41/18 trajectories in English/Arabic), so output-format robustness is a bottleneck, not only language understanding.
method: Dataset translation: R2R instructions, object lists and observations are translated to Arabic with Llama-3.2-90B-text-preview via the Groq API, keeping the original format for NavGPT compatibility.

NavGPT pipeline: visual foundation models turn each viewpoint into text; a Prompt Manager builds the prompt; an LM outputs Thought and Action (next viewpoint ID) with a history summary; the action is executed on the nav graph.
LM swap-in: GPT-4o mini, Llama 3 8B, Phi-3 medium 14B and Jais 30B are hosted on Azure and used zero-shot with per-model prompts to obtain the required output format.
Language conditions: English, Arabic (Arabic thoughts) and Mixed (Arabic data with English thoughts, GPT-4o mini only).

Evaluation: the same 100 R2R val-unseen trajectories in both languages, scored with TL, NE, SR, OSR and SPL, plus qualitative analysis of goal decomposition, sequential consistency and adaptability, including parsing-error and Jais failure cases.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o mini, Llama 3 8B, Phi-3 medium 14B, Jais 30B (all frozen, zero-shot, via NavGPT)
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot); Arabic R2R translations are used only for evaluation
setting.observation: Text descriptions of panoramic views from visual foundation models, plus navigable viewpoints and history

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 sampled trajectories from val-unseen; same set in English and Arabic

numbers_note: Phi-3 medium Arabic row is not listed as an entry but is in Table 1 (18 completed, TL 2.36, NE 8.51, SR/OSR/SPL 0). Metrics are computed only over trajectories where the model produced valid output, so they are not directly comparable across models.
results: GPT-4o mini is the best model, with SR 21.0/SPL 13.0 in English and SR 20.0/SPL 9.34 in Arabic, about 3x Phi-3 (SR 7) and 5x Llama 3 (SR 4). Jais 30B scores 0 SR in both languages, and Phi-3 fails entirely in Arabic. The performance gap between models is larger than the gap between languages.
limitations: Small evaluation of 100 trajectories, with metrics computed over differing numbers of completed trajectories, so cross-model comparison is confounded.
Arabic data are machine-translated by an LLM with no human verification, and perception is text-only via captioners, causing information loss.
Zero-shot only, on a discrete nav graph in simulation (no real robot), with prompt/format parsing failures dominating weaker models.
